title: Jest tests fail on any console.warn or console.error and require UTC
answers: Why are Jest tests failing on React warnings in mitmweb?
How does the mitmweb test harness handle console warnings and errors?
Why do timestamp and date assertions behave differently in local Jest runs?
body:
In `web/setup-jest.js`, `console.warn` and `console.error` are monkey-patched to throw an `Error` immediately:
`console.warn = console.error = function () { err.apply(console, arguments); throw new Error(arguments[0]); };`
Any unhandled React prop mismatch, missing key, or library deprecation warning will immediately fail a test. When rendering components with `web/src/js/__tests__/test-utils.tsx:render`, ensure all required props and mock stores via `web/src/js/__tests__/ducks/tutils.ts:TStore` are fully provided.
Additionally, `web/setup-global-jest.js` forces `process.env.TZ = "UTC"`; local date and time assertions must assume UTC.
applies: Applies to all Jest tests matching `__tests__/.*Spec.(js|ts)x?$` under `web/src/js/`.
says: Web interface automated tests fail whenever any component warning appears in the console.
Frontend test suite fails on developer machines located in non UTC time zones.
Date formatting tests in the web frontend break outside standard international time zones.
Component unit tests fail strictly due to deprecation warnings logged during render.
